President Rodrigo Paz reiterated the policy rationale: "Desde hoy el diésel nos va a costar lo mismo que nos cuesta comprarlo afuera del país... el precio del diésel será igual para todos y va a fluctuar con los precios internacionales."

media.caption: Police and military personnel guard the La Paz–Oruro highway at Villa Remedios to prevent diesel-subsidy blockades, Sept. 21, 2026.

events.title: Bolivia Starts the Week Without Blockades on Main Highways Despite Strike Threats
events.detail: The Administradora Boliviana de Carreteras' road map, updated as of 06:54 Monday, showed no points blocked for social reasons anywhere on the Red Vial Fundamental (national highway network), despite the interdepartmental transport sector's declared 24-hour strike and La Paz's interprovincial federation's threatened departmental blockade, both set for that day. Police and military personnel remained deployed on several main highways, mobilized since early Saturday, to keep traffic moving after the diesel-subsidy elimination. The interdepartmental sector's leadership still had a follow-up assembly scheduled for Tuesday to decide whether to extend pressure measures to 48 or 72 hours if the government did not respond to its demands.

media.caption: A highway on Bolivia's Red Vial Fundamental remains open Monday morning, with no blockade points reported despite strike threats, Sept. 21, 2026.

events.title: El Alto Driver Federation Proposes Indefinite Strike at Tuesday Assembly
events.detail: El Alto's interprovincial driver federation held its ampliado (sector assembly) on Tuesday and moved to propose an indefinite national transport strike, demanding the outright repeal of Decree 5716's diesel-subsidy elimination. Federation leader Eddy Condori said "Estamos exigiendo un paro indefinido. La determinación de la asamblea es la abrogación de este Decreto 5716," while Confederación de Choferes leader Lucio Gómez said the decree forces the sector to review operating costs, warning "¿Quién va a sufrir? El pueblo." The proposal fed into the national confederation's own meeting later that week.

media.caption: El Alto driver federation members gather for their Tuesday assembly to weigh an indefinite strike over Decree 5716, Sept. 22, 2026.

events.title: Police and Military Keep Watch Over Highways as Five Sectors Threaten Pressure Measures
events.detail: Police and military personnel remained deployed on the La Paz-Oruro, Oruro-Cochabamba and El Alto-Tiquina highways, with a visible presence at the Villa Remedios checkpoint, as five sectors — the COB, truck drivers, heavy-transport operators, fuel-tanker operators (cisterneros) and the Six Federations of the Cochabamba tropics — kept pressure measures against Decree 5716 on the table. The Confederación de Transportistas Pesados declared its own state of emergency, demanding the diesel price return to Bs. 9.80/L, and cisterneros kept fuel-loading operations suspended. The government reiterated that the active state of exception would not be used to permit unlawful road blockades.

media.caption: Police and military personnel guard a highway checkpoint as sectors threaten renewed pressure measures over the diesel decree, Sept. 22, 2026.

events.title: Cañeros, Arroceros and Valle Producers Give Government Blockade Ultimatum
events.detail: Sugarcane growers and rice growers concentrated around Montero (Santa Cruz department), together with producers from the Santa Cruz valleys and the Bloque de Transporte Unidos, announced they would begin road blockades unless the government repealed Decree 5716, warning the diesel-subsidy elimination threatens to bankrupt already fuel-scarcity-battered agricultural sectors. The announcement widened the pressure-measure threat beyond La Paz/El Alto transport unions to Santa Cruz's productive sectors.

media.caption: Sugarcane and rice producers near Montero, Santa Cruz, announce blockade plans over the diesel-subsidy elimination, Sept. 2026.

events.title: Confederación Sindical de Choferes Calls National 24-Hour Strike for Monday, Sep 28
events.detail: Following a national meeting in Santa Cruz de la Sierra, the Confederación Sindical de Choferes de Bolivia, led by Lucio Gómez, formally called a 24-hour national transport stoppage for Monday, Sep 28, 2026, threatening to paralyze urban, interprovincial and international transport in rejection of Decree 5716's elimination of the diesel subsidy and the new Bs. 17.95/L price. Gómez said "El lunes no habrá transporte público en el país" and warned the protest could escalate into an indefinite service suspension if demands — including tariff increases to offset operating costs — are not met. The government responded that 80.3% of public-transport vehicles nationwide don't depend exclusively on diesel, and deployed police and military plus regional ministers to explain the measure to affected sectors.

media.caption: Bolivian drivers' confederation leader Lucio Gómez announces a national 24-hour transport strike for Sept. 28, 2026, over the diesel-price hike.

events.title: Lara Declares Himself Acting President During Paz's US Trip, Then Hands Off to Senate's Ávila
events.detail: Vice President Edmand Lara declared himself president in exercise on Monday, Sep 21, as President Rodrigo Paz departed for New York to attend the UN General Assembly (address scheduled Sep 24), invoking Article 169 of the Constitution, which assigns the presidency to the vice president during the head of state's temporary absence, and stating "se va a cumplir la Constitución." The government instead maintains Paz governs remotely under Supreme Decree 5515 (issued Dec 29, 2025), which authorizes him to exercise his functions digitally from abroad — a mechanism used on every prior Paz foreign trip to avoid formally ceding the presidency to Lara. Because Lara himself had an official trip to Paraguay scheduled for Wednesday, Sep 23, he transferred interim authority to Senate president Diego Ávila, a longtime Paz ally, ahead of his own departure, citing the same constitutional succession chain.

media.caption: Vice President Edmand Lara declares himself acting president as Paz departs for New York.

events.title: Constitutional Succession Dispute Escalates as Officials Split Over Ávila vs. Decree 5515
events.detail: The controversy over who holds legitimate presidential authority while Paz and Lara are simultaneously abroad grew through Sep 24. Presidential spokesperson José Luis Gálvez insisted Paz's absence "does not constitute a definitive absence" requiring formal transfer, citing a reported 7-8 hour remote workday and two decrees (on credits and tourism-operator licenses) Paz signed from New York via videoconference cabinet meeting. Legal scholars countered the hierarchy runs the other way: Daniel Valverde, former director of the Political Observatory at Gabriel René Moreno University, said "la CPE es la norma suprema y el decreto es una norma inferior." Prosecutor Roger Mariaca, Santa Cruz Justice Court president Aldo Quezada, Santa Cruz governor Juan Pablo Velasco ("nada está por encima de la Constitución") and civic leader Stello Cochamanidis all recognized Senate president Diego Ávila as legitimate acting president under Article 169. Bolivia's Constitutional Court lacks quorum to resolve the conflict, leaving Decree 5515 in de facto effect despite the legal challenges.

media.caption: Legal experts and officials split over who legitimately holds presidential authority.

events.title: Drivers' Confederation Ratifies 24-Hour Vehicle Withdrawal, Agrees to Dialogue With Government
events.detail: The Confederación Sindical de Choferes de Bolivia confirmed Sep 24 it will proceed with Monday Sep 28's 24-hour national vehicle withdrawal against Decree 5716's diesel-subsidy elimination, while accepting government dialogue, with leaders planning to meet authorities between Tuesday and Wednesday of the following week. The confederation said the action would not include road blockades. The government warned it would use state-of-exception tools if protests escalated into what it considers undemocratic actions.

media.caption: Drivers' confederation confirms the Sep 28 national stoppage and agrees to dialogue with the government.

events.title: Four Driver Federations Break From National Strike, Weakening Monday's Withdrawal
events.detail: Four driver federations — Federación Andina de Choferes 1 de Mayo (El Alto), Transporte Libre de Bolivia, the Federación del Transporte Pesado, and Transporte Chuquiago Mark (La Paz) — announced they will not join the Confederación's Sep 28 vehicle withdrawal, significantly weakening the planned action; taxis, minibuses, trucks and interdepartmental routes tied to these federations are expected to operate normally. Eddy Condori, secretary of the El Alto federation, said the groups still oppose Decree 5716 but will "tomar otro tipo de medidas y estrategias, junto al pueblo" instead. The Federación del Transporte Pesado said it may still join blockade actions later if the government does not address its demands.

media.caption: Four driver federations announce they will not join Monday's vehicle withdrawal.

events.title: Heavy Transport Warns of Border Blockades, El Alto's POR Calls to Join Anti-Diesel Protest
events.detail: Nelson Carrillo, first secretary of the Federación del Transporte Pesado, said his sector was not initially invited to join the Sep 28 action but warned "si no existe acuerdo con Gobierno, nos uniremos a esta solicitud," not ruling out border blockades despite the ongoing state of exception; he accused some transport leaders of having been "comprados" by the government through side meetings. In El Alto, the Pacto de Organizaciones Revolucionarias (POR) called on the population to join the fight against Decree 5716, branding it a "decreto de muerte, hambre y pobreza para las clases populares." Separately, the tanker-operator federation (cisterneros) halted fuel loading and unloading operations pending a resolution with the government.

media.caption: Heavy transport warns of border blockades as El Alto sectors call to join the anti-diesel protest.

events.title: In UN General Assembly Address, Paz Blames Narco-Terrorism for 53 Days of Blockades That Killed 20+
events.detail: In his first address to the UN General Assembly, delivered Sep 24, President Rodrigo Paz said narco-terrorist networks financed the 53 days of blockades that paralyzed Bolivia earlier in the crisis, which he said left more than 20 dead and cut off access to food, medicine and fuel. He argued Bolivia lacks the economic and human resources to fully combat these criminal networks — which he said also draw on smuggling and illegal gold-mining proceeds — and appealed for stronger international cooperation. Alluding to Evo Morales without naming him, Paz said the former president claimed to defend the Pachamama (Mother Earth) while actually destroying it over 20 years, and distinguished the right to protest from attempts to "break the constitutional and democratic framework" of the country.

media.caption: President Paz addresses the UN General Assembly, blaming narco-terrorism for financing 53 days of blockades.
